title: [Lean] Preserve surrounding tape contents during marked writeback
body:
## Coverage

Explicit author-checked context: upstream main 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea; kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918. This generic result does not change the exponent.

Finite coverage: arbitrary equal-width marked words, including width zero, with arbitrary left/right destination spectators, including markers. The left context is stored in reverse zipper order. The unchanged finite-symbol controller copies the source first track into the destination first track, preserves the other track and complete standalone source, returns both local heads and clears initial scratch.

This module derives confinement and lifts every actual step/run through the surrounding destination context. Exact first halt is 7*n+9; every-prefix represented cells are bounded by left.length+2*n+4+right.length, counting all ambient contexts and both local tapes.

Conditional-interface coverage: prepared equal-width source/destination words, reached focus and allocation remain supplied. Overwritten target bits and dirty scratch are not restored. Only destination spectators are added; the source remains standalone.

Full-theorem coverage: no packed metadata client, key search, global travel, selected artifact success, recursive cost bound or whole multiplication/runtime theorem is claimed.

## Evidence and reproduction

One unchanged source, 10,674 bytes, with six complete standard-only axiom probes and no warnings. No additional full-type prints are claimed. Independent exact-source/API and native-terminal acceptance is summarized publicly. The historical uncompiled-candidate comment remains in the source; the hash-bound acceptance supersedes it without changing proof bytes.

README gives an isolated four-module replay with existing Lean 4.21.0, explicit hashes, bounded serial admission and logs. Mathlib is not required. This recipe was inspected but not rerun for publication; no additional CI preflight was performed.

## Overlap and attribution

Three public prerequisites are reused without copying: PR #1840 at 3f1b0641d5866f9d0b6cdd8e46db416fed6c5645 and PR #1933 at ad36a85e226f72fe9cb300236cc004049394c389. The new contribution derives destination confinement and spectator preservation for the existing writeback controller. It follows the marked-XOR confinement method from PR #1921; no broad novelty claim is made.

James Chang with OpenAI assistance, Apache-2.0; predecessor attribution retained. Next useful step is the already separate packed source-refresh client and paid global access/return composition.
